intro: SYNC Manufacturing provides custom rubber molding, rubber-to-metal bonding, engineered plastics, and precision manufacturing solutions for valve OEMs and industrial flow-control equipment manufacturers.

Our manufacturing expertise supports critical components used in municipal water distribution, wastewater treatment, industrial processing, utilities, fire-protection equipment, and fluid-handling systems.

From rubber-encapsulated valve wedges and bonded eccentric plugs to molded check-valve flappers, resilient seals, and engineered plastic valve components, SYNC combines material knowledge, manufacturing processes, and application-specific engineering support.

With capabilities in compression molding, transfer molding, rubber compounding, rubber-to-metal bonding, thermoset molding, and thermoplastic injection molding, we help customers develop and manufacture components engineered for their operating environments.
Whether you're developing a new valve component, evaluating an alternative manufacturing process, or qualifying an additional domestic supplier, our team can help assess your requirements.

sections.heading: Manufacturing Solutions for the Valve Industry

blocks.text: Valve components operate in environments where sealing performance, material compatibility, mechanical integrity, and manufacturing consistency are critical.
A molded component may be exposed to repeated pressure cycles, water-treatment chemicals, abrasive materials, changing temperatures, mechanical loads, and extended service intervals.
Successful manufacturing requires more than producing a component to dimensional specifications.
It requires understanding how the material, molded geometry, bonding interface, and manufacturing process contribute to the performance of the finished valve.
SYNC's experience in engineered elastomers, rubber-to-metal bonding, and precision plastics manufacturing allows us to support valve OEMs with a broad range of component manufacturing requirements.

Eccentric Plug Valve Components
Eccentric plug valves are commonly used in wastewater treatment, municipal infrastructure, and industrial flow-control systems.
Many resilient-seated designs incorporate an elastomer facing or encapsulation bonded to a metal plug.
The rubber provides the sealing interface while the metal substrate supplies the structural support required by the valve design.
SYNC's rubber-to-metal bonding and molding expertise supports the evaluation of custom eccentric plug components requiring:

Controlled rubber coverage and sealing geometry

sections.heading: Rubber-to-Metal Bonding for Critical Valve Applications

blocks.text: Rubber-to-metal bonding is one of SYNC's core specialties in flow-control manufacturing.
The process creates an integrated component by joining an engineered elastomer to a prepared metal substrate.
Depending on part design, bonding may be achieved during vulcanization using appropriate adhesive systems or through other approved bonding and encapsulation techniques.
Successful bonding requires coordination of several manufacturing disciplines:
Metal Substrate Preparation
The condition, cleanliness, geometry, and surface preparation of the metal insert influence adhesion and manufacturing consistency.
Bonding System Selection
Primers, adhesives, and application methods must be compatible with the selected elastomer, metal substrate, and molding conditions.
Custom Rubber Compounding
Rubber formulations are selected around sealing performance, hardness, compression set, mechanical loads, chemical exposure, and operating temperature.
Tooling & Mold Design
Mold design must address material flow, insert location, venting, critical sealing geometry, and consistent coverage of the metal substrate.
Molding & Vulcanization
Controlled temperature, pressure, and curing conditions help establish the required elastomer properties and bonded interface.
Inspection & Validation
Inspection and testing requirements may include dimensional verification, material properties, adhesion evaluation, and customer-specific qualification procedures.

By integrating these considerations into the component manufacturing process, SYNC helps customers evaluate the complete bonded assembly rather than treating the rubber and metal as separate manufacturing requirements.

sections.heading: Engineered Rubber Materials for Valve Applications

blocks.text: Selecting the correct elastomer is essential to long-term sealing performance and component durability.
SYNC's custom rubber compounding expertise supports evaluation of materials for different operating environments.
EPDM
Commonly evaluated for water-service applications because of its resistance to water, ozone, weathering, and many environmental conditions.
The suitability of a specific EPDM formulation depends on temperature, treatment chemicals, operating conditions, and applicable requirements.
Nitrile Rubber (NBR)
Commonly selected for compatibility with petroleum-based oils, fuels, and certain industrial fluids.
Nitrile may be appropriate for valve applications where resistance to specified oils or hydrocarbons is important.
Neoprene (CR)
Provides balanced mechanical properties and resistance to selected environmental and chemical conditions.
It may be considered for wastewater and industrial sealing applications, depending on service requirements.
Natural Rubber (NR)
Offers elasticity, resilience, and useful mechanical properties for selected dynamic and sealing applications.
Silicone Rubber
Provides flexibility across a broad temperature range and resistance to environmental aging.
Silicone materials may be appropriate for selected specialized sealing applications, subject to fluid compatibility and mechanical requirements.
Fluoroelastomers (FKM)
Specialized elastomers used for certain applications involving elevated temperatures and aggressive chemical environments.

faq.q: Does SYNC manufacture rubber-to-metal bonded valve components?

a.text: Yes. SYNC has established rubber-to-metal bonding and molding expertise applicable to custom valve plugs, resilient sealing components, and other engineered bonded assemblies.
Specific component designs are evaluated against available tooling, equipment, materials, and customer requirements.

faq.q: Can SYNC manufacture rubber-encapsulated metal valve components?

a.text: Yes. SYNC offers manufacturing processes suitable for selected rubber-over-metal applications, including compression and transfer molding.

faq.q: What types of valves can use molded rubber components?

a.text: Common examples include eccentric plug valves, resilient-seated gate valves, check valves, butterfly valves, and selected hydrant and specialty valve designs.

faq.q: What rubber materials are commonly used in valve components?

a.text: EPDM, nitrile, neoprene, natural rubber, silicone, and specialty elastomers may be considered depending on the application.

faq.q: Can SYNC develop custom rubber compounds for valve applications?

a.text: Yes. SYNC has in-house compounding and material-development expertise to support specialized performance requirements.

faq.q: Can SYNC manufacture engineered plastic valve components?

a.text: Yes. SYNC offers thermoplastic and thermoset molding, tooling, and machining capabilities applicable to selected valve and pump components.
SYNC can evaluate components intended for drinking-water systems. Material, component, and finished-product certification requirements must be established for each program.

faq.q: Can SYNC support existing tooling transfers or second-source programs?

a.text: Yes. Our teams can review existing drawings, tooling, material specifications, and manufacturing requirements to evaluate the feasibility of transferring or qualifying a production program.

faq.q: Does SYNC support large rubber-molded valve components?

a.text: SYNC has large-format compression molding resources. Maximum manufacturable dimensions depend on the component geometry, tooling, press configuration, and available capacity.
